label: Incriminating Character of the Item Was Not Immediately Apparent
motion_heading: The Plain-View Doctrine Does Not Apply Because the Incriminating Character of the Item Was Not Immediately Apparent

sentences.text: A warrantless seizure of an item in plain view is permitted only if the item's incriminating character is immediately apparent.
That requires probable cause to believe the item is contraband or evidence of a crime, without any further search.

practice_notes: Look for any step the officer took before being sure what the item was — a field test, a closer look, a question to your client. Each one suggests the character wasn't immediately apparent.

If police say they saw more than one item in plain view, this section treats them together. If the facts differ by item (e.g. where the officer was, or whether it was obvious what the item was), consider a separate argument for each.
